lines: Every fish is now one of a kind. Each has its own weight, and its size and price follow it: a light fish sells for up to a fifth less than its rarity's price and a heavy one up to a fifth more (Common $10 to $14, Legendary $800 to $1,200). The first time you catch a fish it gets a number, like "King Salmon #5", which is its name until you give it one, and the catch card shows its price and a gold "New!" for the first of a kind. Fish of a kind you have caught now show faintly in the pond as themselves; kinds you have never caught are still dark shadows. Tap a fish with anything but the Fishing Rod to open its menu: see its weight and price, Pet it, Nudge it, give it a name (a named fish no longer swims off) or Release it for good. In Storage each kind of fish shows what they are worth together, Sell sells the lightest first, and tapping the row lists every fish with Sell, Let go and Rename; a fish you let go keeps its number and name, and catching it again gives no XP. Fish already in Storage got numbers and weights.

The album cover on Now Playing (Settings → Sound) now changes with the season of the music: each season has its own cover in the style of the season-change title, with its icon and name glowing in the season's color over the farm's hills, sky and weather (Spring petals, Summer sunlight, Fall leaves, Winter snow). When the season turns, the new cover fades in as the music crosses over.

When a chicken or farm animal eats one of your crops on its own, it is now fed just as if you had fed it by hand: five minutes Well Fed, making its milk, eggs, wool or fertilizer 25% faster, with the Feed countdown and boosted bar in its menu. An animal that is already Well Fed is full and leaves your crops alone. Crops eaten this way still don't count toward feeding quests.

Eggs are now picked up like crops, never mistaken for the hen: tapping an egg lying beside a hen goes to the egg, not her menu (tap the hen herself for that). Only the Bucket collects it; tapping an egg with any other tool, or holding a finger on it, says "Use the Bucket from the Harvest tool to collect eggs". Nothing can be planted, built, fertilized or set down on top of an egg (dragging seeds or terrain across one just skips its tile), and trees and rocks no longer grow over one.
The song "Sheep" has been taken out of Spring's music.

Each season in the song list (Settings → Sound, the list button on Now Playing) now has a shuffle button, off to begin with. With it on, that season's music starts on a random song every time the season begins, whether you open the game into it or the season changes, then plays its songs in a random order, a fresh one each time round. Songs you have unchecked stay out, and you can still tap a song to play it. Reset to Default turns shuffle off.

About five soft, slightly see-through pixel clouds now drift slowly and smoothly across the farm with the wind, each casting a soft shadow on the ground a couple of tiles away. They sit over the farm itself, moving with the ground as you drag and zoom, are already there when the farm opens, and new ones float in from the edge of the farm as others drift off the far side. They turn grey and hurry along in the rain (with no shadows, and a couple more of them), whiter over Winter's snow, and moonlit blue at night. They fade away when you zoom in any closer than the farm opens at, never get in the way of taps, and hold still with Reduce Motion. Turn them off with the new Clouds switch in Settings → Graphics.

Tapping an animal now opens a small menu that fits what it shows, with the farm still in view and the animal ringed in a soft white glow that follows it as it walks. Under its name, each kind of animal has its own little personality line, such as "Makes milk, can't read" for a cow or "Just a little baby" for every baby. Below that, animals that grow up or make something have a line saying what they are up to, such as "Next milk in 2m 40s" or "Grows up in 12m 40s", with a blue bar; once its milk, egg or wool is waiting the line turns green and says which tool collects it, such as "Milk waiting · use the Bucket". Below are Feed, Pet and Nudge. Feed shows Wheat and lights up green when the animal is hungry and you have food: tap it to pick a food from your storage, favorite first. While the animal is Well Fed, Feed counts down the rest of its meal and the bar turns purple with little arrows racing along it; with no food stored it says "No Food". Cats, dogs, roosters and grown ducks show only their personality line, and cats, dogs and grown ducks have no Feed in the menu, but you can still drop food on them. Collect what animals give with the Harvest tool on the farm. A button at the bottom sells ducks and ducklings for $25 or releases any other animal, and asks first. You can now release your pet too: its Pet House stays empty until you choose a new pet in the house's menu.

Thunder now rolls through every rain shower, loud enough to hear clearly over the rain, in Spring, Summer and Fall, about every minute, in four different rolls from near to far, never the same one twice in a row. Lightning is rare: only about one shower in ten brings a soft flash across the farm now and then (not with Reduce Motion). Winter snow stays quiet. Thunder follows the Ambience volume and fades away when the rain stops.
The Shed now costs $500 (was $2,500) and the Silo $1,500 (was $7,000), so more storage is easy to add as your farm grows.

The loading page now checks for a newer version of the game just before syncing with iCloud, so an update message is ready sooner. It waits at most a second and a half and says "Checking for update…" when it takes a moment; offline or on a slow connection, the farm opens as usual and the check finishes in the background.

Each season's music now plays in a chosen order, opening gently, mixing calmer and livelier songs and ending on its calmest, instead of in alphabetical order. A new list button in the top right of the Now Playing card (Settings → Sound) shows every season's songs in the order they play, with the song playing highlighted. Uncheck a song to leave it out of its season (each season keeps at least one), tap a song of the season playing to play it, and tap Rearrange to drag songs into a new order or into another season. Reset to Default puts every song back. Your choices are kept on this device.

The midnight wave now brings more of what your farm is missing for your level: with plenty of trees and rocks it brings Copper Veins instead, a farm short of trees or rocks gets more of them, and Silver, Gold, Ruby and Sapphire Veins turn up more often the closer you get to the level you can smelt or cut them.
Settings → About has a new Credits page naming who made the game's art, music and sounds: each work with its author and licence, and a tap on its title opens its page in Safari.

When a newer version of the game is ready (a new TestFlight build, or a new version on the App Store), a message says so once your farm has opened, with Update and Ignore. Update takes you to TestFlight or the App Store; after Ignore, that version never asks again, and a yellow pulsing "!" sits between your money and your Level until you update. Tap it to see the message again. With Reduce Motion it stays still.

Every chicken and farm animal's favorite food is now Wheat, and every cat and dog's is Salmon, in place of a different favorite crop for each kind. Feeding quests now read "Hand-feed 10 favorite foods to animals from the Sheep Barn" and count Wheat (or Salmon); quests you already have keep their progress. The animal menu no longer has a favorite line.

Every building's page in the Build menu now has a short line under its picture saying what it does, such as "Spawns cows that provide milk for recipes" or "Offers optional quests for extra XP". The Shed and Silo say how many storage slots they add (50 and 150), and the Pet House reads "A home for your furry friend".
Every building's page in the Build menu now has a short line under its picture saying what it does, such as "Spawns cows that provide milk for recipes" or "Offers optional quests for extra XP".

Four new songs join Summer's music: Farm Music by migfus20, Another August by The Cynic Project (cynicmusic.com / pixelsphere.org), Costal Town by Hitctrl and Sunset Plains by Yoiyami (all from OpenGameArt.org).
Crickets now sing softly under the music on Spring, Summer and Fall nights, rising as it gets dark and fading away at dawn; Winter nights stay quiet under the snow. They follow the Ambience volume.

The Shed and Silo pictures under the Storage bar are now in full colour as soon as you unlock them, built or not, with a small count on the corner of how many you have out of the most you can build, like "0/4" or "2/4" (gold once you have them all). A picture stays grey with no count until you reach its level, and tapping one still opens it in the Build menu.

A meal fed by hand now makes an animal give its milk, goat milk, wool, fertilizer or eggs 25% faster for its five minutes, instead of twice as fast, and its menu shows the quicker time while it is Well Fed. An animal still holds only one thing at a time: once it is ready it waits for you to collect it, fed or not, and makes no start on the next one until you do. Babies, ducklings and chicks included, also grow up 25% faster while fed, and a fed pet is 25% more likely to ripen the crop it stands on, instead of twice.

Seasons now change at 6 AM, once it is fully light, on the day they are due, instead of at midnight. Crops, weather, music and the ground all change with it, and each season still lasts 7 days. If you were away past 6 AM on that day, the change plays when you come back; picking a season on the Time sheet still changes it straight away.

When a new season sweeps in, its own weather is already there behind the gust, as if through a window: Winter's snow is falling and Fall's leaves or Spring's petals are in the air, while the old season's weather keeps falling and blowing on the side the gust hasn't reached yet. Nothing freezes while it sweeps: animals, water, smoke, lights, fireflies, trees and everything you do keep moving on both sides, each tree, building and crop turning into its new look as the gust passes over it. The gust carries fewer snowflakes of its own now that Winter's snow shows through.

Every animal now eats any food you feed it by hand: pets, chickens (roosters and chicks too) and every farm animal, ducks included, take any crop, any fruit basket from your fruit trees, any fish, eggs, milk, flour, bread, cheese and anything made from them, such as juice, preserves, pie, soup and pickles. Pick a food in Storage or the Decorate tool's list and drag it onto an animal. Every meal gives the same five-minute boost as before; only an animal's favorite food counts toward feeding quests.

A new season now sweeps across the farm in a gust from top left to bottom right, with a glittering edge in the season's colors and petals, sun motes, leaves or snow trailing behind, while you keep playing. The season's name rises into focus from below once the gust has passed it, lingers a few moments and sinks away; the music fades into the new season's and a soft whoosh and chime plays. It waits until the level-up and day summary are closed, plays after the farm loads if the season changed while the game was closed, and also plays when you pick a season on the Time sheet. With Reduce Motion the new season simply fades in. This replaces the full-screen splash and "is here" message.
When you move a building, decoration or tree, the arrows round it are now chunky pixel chevrons that match the farm's art and hop gently outward; the one you drag turns gold.
When you chop a tree or break a rock or ore vein, its count and bar now show just above your finger, so your finger no longer hides how close it is to coming down.
Hide Grid Lines Beyond in Settings → Graphics now starts at 2.0×, so grid lines fade away sooner as you zoom out; Reset to Defaults sets it there too. A zoom you already picked is kept.
Tapping an animal that already has a name now offers Rename instead of Name, and its naming box says "Rename it".

Seasons now last 7 days each, instead of 14, going Spring, Summer, Fall, Winter and round again. A season you pick on the Time sheet also lasts 7 days from that day. A farm you already have keeps the season it is in when you open it, and its next change comes within 7 days.

In the tutorial, the steps that find and gather from a tree, rock, ore vein or fish now pick one and keep pointing at that same one, glowing gold, until the step is done, instead of jumping to whichever is nearest as you look around; another is picked only if it disappears.
The tutorial no longer puts red dots on the buttons and rows it points at; they swell with a gold glow instead.
In the tutorial, "Pinch to zoom in on the tree" (or rock, ore vein or fish) now shows two fingers spreading apart over it, the opposite of the zoom-out step's pinch.
The tutorial now only points you at small trees, small rocks and Copper Veins to chop and mine, even when a bigger tree or rock is closer. If none are left, small ones turn up near your field.
Chimney smoke is a little thicker where it leaves the chimney, so it shows against any roof or ground, and still fades out as it rises.
Lanterns come in a new Leaf green colour, with green glass and a soft green light at night.

At night a Lantern's lit glass, the buildings' lit windows and the Christmas lights are now hidden behind anything standing in front of them, such as a rock, tree or building, instead of shining through it; only their soft glow still spreads over everything.
Tapping a hen now says about how long until her next egg, or that her egg is ready; farm animals say "Milk in 2 min" or "Milk ready" in the same way.
The Storage menu shows a Shed and a Silo under its fill bar in place of the text, greyed until you have one; tap either to see its page from the Build menu.
The Bucket now starts on Sell on a new farm, like the Scythe, so eggs, milk, wool and fruit sell the moment you gather them; switch either to Store whenever you like.
When a farm can't be opened, the message now says to retry or restore a backup, which the Load Game menu's farm options offer.

Settings → Timelapse has a Picture size menu, from Smallest (1024 × 1024) to Largest (4096 × 4096), showing about how much room each picture and each day takes; it sets the size of both timelapse screenshots and Screenshot Farm photos, which start at Medium (2048 × 2048).
Settings → Timelapse can take up to three screenshots a day: add, change or remove capture times, and a day's screenshots play in time order.
Timelapse screenshots, and the video made from them, no longer show tile grid lines.

Moving a building, tree, fruit tree or decoration has a Nudge button that opens a Nudge pad, like the Lantern's, under the Move menu, shifting just its picture a quarter of a tile toward any side or corner; the picture stays nudged when a fruit tree is picked, a pet hurries a plant along or a wild tree grows.
While a timelapse plays or is paused, pinch to zoom in on the farm and drag to look around; double-tap to zoom in on a spot or back out.

Screenshot Farm pictures and timelapse screenshots now show the farm in the middle with the same margin of empty space on every side, so a Silo, barn, House or tall tree on the farm's edge is no longer cut off.

Settings → Timelapse has Export Video: it turns your farm's daily screenshots into a short video, each day a second (quicker for long timelapses), and Share Video then sends it to Photos, Messages or any other app.

Moving something gives it a soft glow round its shape, white where it fits and red where it can't go, and a gold handle on each side; tap a handle to step one tile, or drag a handle or the thing itself to move it any way a tile at a time.

The Move menu is now a small glass tag hanging under the thing being placed or moved (above it near the bottom of the screen), with its picture and name, whether it fits or why not, a bin for something already standing, and Nudge, Place and Cancel; Place is greyed out while it can't go there, and the bin asks right in the tag.
Both Houses' brick chimneys now meet the roof without a dark seam line, in every season.

Settings → Sound has a new Now Playing card: an album cover with the song's name and artist, previous, play/pause and next buttons, and the music volume slider, replacing the old Music slider and song line.

Animals no longer get hungry: they give their eggs, milk, wool and fertilizer at their usual pace without needing to eat, and the hungry picture over their heads is gone. Instead grown chickens and farm animals are now and then pests: one that wanders onto a crop may eat it, at most one crop a day each; fence your fields to keep them out. Feeding favorites by hand still gives a short boost.
Hens now lay their eggs on the ground wherever they happen to be walking, instead of carrying them over their heads; collect them with the Bucket where they lie.

Whenever a farm becomes Spring or Fall, whether it loads, you open another farm, pick a season, the season turns on its own or you return to the app, the first petals or leaves now cross the screen straight away, instead of a minute later.
Spring's grass has 15% more wildflowers.
The Axe now chops a tree wherever you tap or swipe on its picture, its leaves included, not only on the tile under its trunk.
The first-level House no longer hangs a second strand of Christmas lights along the beam above its door, in any season.

The House's chimney now smokes, at both levels: a soft, puffy plume that drifts with the wind, with a soft curl of smoke rising smoothly straight up about a second after the last one fades, turning left and right by turns. The Stone Oven's flue smokes the same way, smaller, while it bakes. The smoke is a darker grey in Winter so it shows on the snow, thinner in the rain, glows faintly warm at the chimney at night, and stands still with Reduce Motion.

New Lantern at the top of the Decorate menu ($25, 4 Logs and 2 Copper Ore): a small wooden lantern on one tile that casts a soft, cosy wash of coloured light all round it at night over the ground, buildings, trees and crops nearby, flickering softly like the building windows (steady with Reduce Motion). Tap it to pick its color (Candle yellow, Warm amber, Soft white, Pale blue or Rose; its glass is colored to match), its Brightness (Low, Medium or High), its Range (Short, Medium or Long), its Power (Auto at night and in rain, Always on or Always off) and an Effect (Flicker or Steady) and a nudge to any of nine spots within its tile. A lantern put away with the Axe keeps its settings.

A decoration, tree, crop, rock or animal standing on the same bottom row as a building is now drawn on top of the building instead of behind it, while a fence there stays behind it (the building's Christmas lights stay with the building).

Every tree and Christmas Tree, at every size, now stands on just the one tile under its trunk, drawn centred on it, with its leaves spreading over the tiles around, which stay free for animals, paths and anything else. Trees on your farm move onto the tile under their trunk.

Planting or moving a tree can no longer replace another tree by accident: a tree, decoration, building or path can't go on the tile a tree or Christmas Tree stands on, and a farm that already had two trees on one spot keeps one and pays back any of yours it removes.

Bigger trees give far more logs: Small trees 3, Medium 7, Big 15 and Huge 30, so a new farm's forest holds enough to build everything once. A first Axe takes one swing per log, so big trees take many swings; upgraded Axes still halve that and then fell any tree in one.

New farms start with fewer plain rocks and many more ore veins, including a Ruby and two Sapphire veins, and together they hold enough stone and ore to build every building and decoration once. Rocks and veins now give twice as much or more (Small, Medium and Big rocks 5, 10 and 15 stones; Copper veins 12 ore, gems 6), and a first Pickaxe takes one swing for each stone or ore it gives.
The midnight wave glows brighter in every season: each of its pixels now has its own soft halo in its own color, so the pixels stand out clearly, even on Winter's snow.

Night window lights are softer and more natural in every season: the House (door window included), Shed, Rabbit Hutch, Sheep, Goat and Pig Barns and the Luxury Barns now glow from a lamp inside with the frames and bars showing, and the Stone Oven's fire glows up from its hearth inside the arch, still flickering. Every building's night light, windows and doorways alike, now pulses gently like the Chicken Coop's, each building in its own time so the farm never pulses together (they stay steady with Reduce Motion).
Animals and pets can now walk behind trees and Christmas Trees, wandering into the tiles under the leaves and disappearing behind them; only the row a tree stands on still blocks them.

The seasons' music is reshuffled: Spring gains Gymnopédie No.1 and loses Path To Lake Land and Synthwave 15k, Summer gains Evening Harmony, Fall now opens with Memories Of A Lost Autumn and gains Path To Lake Land, and Winter now opens with Winter Is Coming and gains Synthwave 15k, Wanderer's Tale, No More Magic and The Fallen. Minuet, Pineapple Under The Sea, Whispering Woods and Strange Worlds are gone from the game.
The farm can now be dragged much further at any zoom, until most of it is off screen; a strip of it always stays in view so you can drag it back.

Christmas lights in Winter: colored string lights hang along the roof edges of the Houses, Barns, Luxury Barns, Stable, Silo, Market Stands, Shed, Rabbit Hutch, Chicken Coop and Pet House, and at night and in the rain their bulbs glow like the Christmas Tree's, and now and then a few bulbs at a time, never neighbors together, swell with a soft glow of their color and settle back, so the string gently twinkles without ever blinking (with Reduce Motion they stay solid). Settings > Graphics > Christmas Lights holds three choices: Power (Always On, which also glows softly by day and is how new players start, Always Off, which keeps the strands but no glow, or Auto, which glows at night and in rain), Pattern (Twinkling or Solid) and All Year (Yes shows them in every season, No only in Winter). Your earlier Solid/Twinkling and Always show choices carry over.
Spring now has flower petals on the wind: now and then a gust carries a few small pink, white and pale yellow petals tumbling across the farm, just like Fall's leaves.

New Settings > Graphics > Weather effects switch, on to start with: turn it off to hide the falling rain and snow and the darker tint under them, the Fall leaves, the Spring petals and the curls of wind. The weather itself carries on, so the animals still go in when it pours and the rain is still heard.

Snow now falls all through Winter, day and night: lighter most of the time and heavier in the 2 PM to 5 PM storm. The animals still only go in, and windows only light up for the weather, during those hours. Rain and snow also keep falling when the wind changes direction, instead of stopping partway.

Rocks, ore veins and the small standing decorations (Pumpkins, Decorative Watermelon, Small Hay Pile, Scarecrow, Crop and Wooden Signs, Milk Cans, Milk Baskets, Wooden Stool, Empty Basket, Dressmaker Display, Trunk, Pet Bowl and Weathercock) now stand up off the ground: the base of each, where it really meets the ground (a rock's foot rather than the shadow under it, a pumpkin's round bottom, a sign's or scarecrow's post), sits on the middle of its tile and the rest rises over the tile behind it, the way trees do, drawn in front of whatever stands there. Each still takes up only its own tile, which is where it is tapped, mined or moved, and butterflies land on the thing itself.

Three new paths in the Terrain tool, Wood Plank Path, Brick Path and Herringbone Brick Path, each $2 a tile from the start: square, a step below the grass like every path, with the same soft shadow under the grass, and clear of snow in Winter.
Paths stay clear of snow in Winter: the dirt paths, in every shade, and the stone path look just as they do in Summer, with no frost.

New decoration: the Christmas Tree, a green pine hung with colored string lights and a star, in Small, Medium, Big and Huge, for $80, 8 logs and a Copper Ore. Like a planted pine it takes up only the row it stands on, one tile for Small and two for the others, and rises over the tiles behind it, which stay free. It wears snow in Winter, and at night and in the rain its bulbs and star light up with a soft colored glow, a few of its bulbs at a time swelling with a soft glow while the star shines steadily.

About half the trees on the farm, of every kind and size, and the Christmas Trees, are now drawn facing the other way, so the woods look less uniform. Each tree always faces the same way. Trees are now tapped, chopped and picked up only on the row they stand on, and the outline when planting or moving one shows just that row.
Lit windows at night and in the rain now sit exactly on each building's windows in every season, including the redrawn Fall and Winter Houses, the grey Luxury Barn in Fall and the Shed in Fall.

Buildings with no windows now glow from their doorway at night and in the rain, in every season: the Silo shed's door has four glass panes that light up amber, the Stable's stalls glow with soft lamplight on their wood, and the Stone Oven's mouth glows the orange of the old door torch. The Chicken Coop's and Pet House's doorways glow amber, strongest at the top of the opening and fading to a faint glow at the floor, with no light on the step.

Five more songs join the seasons' music: Synthwave 15k by The Cynic Project (cynicmusic.com) and Nostalgic RPG Town Hub Theme by antonioraymond71 in Spring, "The Fallen" and "Memories of a Lost Autumn", composed by Jonathan Shaw (www.jshaw.co.uk), in Fall, and Winter is Coming by KipperFalcon in Winter (all from OpenGameArt.org).

Four new songs join the seasons' music: Path to Lake Land by Alexandr Zhelanov in Spring, No More Magic by HorrorPen and Autumn by maou in Fall, and Sleep & Snow by Tsorthan Grove in Winter (all from OpenGameArt.org).

Every kind of ground now has proper edges, on three levels: grass and fields on top, every path (the dirt paths, the stone path and the new wood and brick paths) a step down, ponds lowest. Fields look just as they always did, flat and square with no edge or highlight of their own, even where a path runs beside them, which sits a step below in its soft shadow. Every step down has a clean edge with one soft shadow on the lower side, the same under the grass or a field on every path, and gentler on a pond. Dirt paths sit just inside their tiles in gentle swells with rounded corners, paths of every kind meet each other dead straight and level, with no shadow or line between them, the stone, wood and brick paths have square sides and corners, their cobbles, boards and bricks running cleanly up to their top edge, and a path or field in a lake meets the water directly with a little overhang on its south side, the dirt path's corners rounded and the others square, with no snow specks along the water's edge in Winter.
Oaks have fresher spring leaves and olive-gold fall leaves.
In Winter the apple, banana, lemon, orange and peach trees keep their summer leaves and fruit colors, with just a light line of snow along the tops of the crown and branches.
Spring's wildflowers are twice as big, so you can spot them without zooming right in.

Winter snow is a cooler steel blue again, like it used to be: the snowy ground keeps its texture in five icy blue-grey shades, and the snow on roofs, trees, fences, crops, rocks and decorations is a touch bluer to match.
Ripe wheat now has a dab of snow on its ears in Winter, like the other crops.

In Winter every oak and birch, of every size and leaf color, now has the same fine, twiggy bare branches with a thin line of snow as the big green ones, and the Sheep, Goat and Pig Barns, both Houses, the Silo (tower and tower with shed), both Market Stands and the Stable have new snow on their roofs, and the Rabbit Hutch's front beam is now under snow too. The Winter House has lost its two stray twigs and its roof line is closed, and the Winter Chicken Coop has new hand-shaded snow on its roof. In Fall the Sheep, Goat and Pig Barns, the grey Luxury Barn, the Rabbit Hutch, both Houses, the Stable, the Silo and both Market Stands have new fallen leaves on their roofs.
Fall grass is a warmer golden olive.

The House and the Luxury House now have a brick chimney in every season, built from the Brick Path's bricks with a grey stone cap, and snow on top in Winter. The House's Winter chimney moves from the ridge to the left side of the roof.

In Spring about 300 tiny wildflowers dot the grass in white, yellow, orange, violet, sky blue and red, always in the same places on a farm. They only grow on bare grass and vanish under anything you put down.
Rain and snow are lighter on the phone and look the same

There are now four seasons, Spring, Summer, Fall and Winter, of 14 days each, and they now change by themselves: when a new season comes the screen closes and opens again as it does when you change farms, so nothing pops in, and one that came while the game was closed is there when you open it. New farms start in Summer. You can still pick a season on the Time sheet, and it then lasts 14 days from that day. The green look you know is now Summer, so a farm you had in Spring opens in Summer looking just as before, and Spring is new to see in Progress. Summer keeps the original music and Spring has its own four songs. The midnight wave now mixes colors: green and yellow in Spring, green in Summer, orange and red in Fall, and cyan, blue and light blue in Winter, drawn over the snow so it shows. The water takes a slightly different shade each season: fresher in Spring, greener in Fall and cooler in Winter.
At night the buildings' windows now glow warm amber, with a soft light just round each one, in place of the torch by every building's door.

Dirt paths are redrawn as trodden earth with soft grassy edges that join up into runs, corners, crossings and ends, and now come in three shades (Dark, the usual Dirt Path, and Light) at 2 coins a tile. Paths you already laid become the middle shade, and different paths meet with no grass between them. In spring they gather petals and sprouts, in fall leaves, and in winter they are frozen earth between swept snow banks.
Spring has its own look: fresher grass, oaks in new leaf (the blue-green one with a little cream blossom), fresh-green birches and pines with light new tips.

Fall and Winter have new art: Fall has calm late-green grass, russet oaks, gold birches and buildings in their own colors with a few leaves on every roof and ledge; Winter has soft blue-white snow, snow to the edges of every roof, green pines under snow, bare oaks and white-barked birches with snow along their limbs, and crops with a dab of snow. The big green oak and birch in Winter now have finer, twiggier branches, the Chicken Coop wears a thick drift of snow on its roof, and in Fall it has a few small leaves on its roof. Winter snow now also lies on the newer crops, the ore veins, the Dairy and Cheese Cellar (which get a few Fall leaves too) and the bigger farmyard decorations: hay, wood piles, troughs, mangers, crates, sacks, chests and every sign. The Dairy's machine keeps its snow or leaves while it works.
The Luxury Barn's metal roof no longer has teal streaks, in every color and season.
New farms have a few fewer trees (about 390), and trees of any size, rocks of any size and any ore can now be found anywhere outside the clearing round your first field.

Each midnight, wild trees may grow a size if they have room, wild rocks grow from small to medium to big, and small silver veins grow into full ones. New wild trees, rocks and ore veins appear on empty ground anywhere on the farm, until the farm has about 390 wild trees, 50 rocks and 5 veins. Trees you planted and rocks you placed never grow and don't count. Existing farms keep their layout and start growing from their next midnight.
The Tree Density option is gone from new farms and from a farm's Properties; shared seeds now end in three numbers (like B111), and older seeds still work.
Every pet now has its own sign in Decorations: the Dog Sign comes in all nine dogs, each breed in each of its colors, and a new Cat Sign shows each of the nine cats.
Three new cats can move into a Pet House: Tabby, Tuxedo and Tortoiseshell, so there are now as many cats as dogs.

An upgraded Axe now gives extra logs from every wild tree (1 more at Level 2, 2 more at Level 3), and an upgraded Pickaxe extra stones from every wild rock the same way. Ore from veins is unchanged, and trees you planted and rocks you placed still give nothing. The tool and upgrade pages show the new amounts.

Tapping the iCloud cloud on Load Game now opens a small bubble from it that says what syncing is doing, when your farms last synced and anything wrong or waiting on you, and it closes by itself after a good sync.
At most 10 butterflies are on the farm at once, counting the ones you released, like the fireflies: with 10 released no wild ones come out. How often they appear and their colors are unchanged.
Butterflies you release now stay within 1 tile of where you let them go, in every direction including diagonals, like the fireflies.
Fireflies you set free now roam anywhere within 1 tile of where you let them go, in every direction including diagonals.

Every night now has exactly 10 fireflies, three of them colored and the rest orange, coming out at set moments through the night; at most 10 are on the farm at once, counting the ones you set free. Each colored one is Uncommon (44%), Rare (28%), Epic (16%), Legendary (9%) or Shifting (3%), and white Common fireflies no longer come out (ones you already caught stay in Storage), so Progress no longer asks for one.

In winter, curls of wind end in frost: ones whose swirl curls up twinkle with little ice-blue stars at its tip, and ones that curl down shed a few ice crystals that drift off and fall as the swirl fades.

On iPad, buttons such as Place and Cancel, Upgrade, Select and Close, messages and the newer-save banner no longer stretch across the whole screen: they keep a sensible width and sit centred, and the newer-save banner now shows at the top. iPhone is unchanged.

Any Axe can fell any tree and any Pickaxe can break any rock or mine any ore vein again: a better tool just takes fewer swings (Axe 1 takes 3 to 6 by tree size, Pickaxe 1 takes 4 to 12 for rocks and 6 for veins, Level 2 about half that, Level 3 one). Tree sizes no longer show an Axe level, Market Stand quests can ask for any ore whatever your Pickaxe, and the tool pages and level-up screen say how much faster each level is.
The tutorial now says "Find a tree" and "Find a rock" instead of asking for a small one, since any Axe or Pickaxe cuts every size.

You can now zoom out much further, on iPhone and iPad alike, until the whole farm is a small square about an inch wide. The farm now always stays on screen: zoomed out you can slide it anywhere but never off the edge, and zoomed in you can pan only a little past its edges.

While you play, a banner tells you when a newer save of your farm arrives from another device, with a Load button (the copy it replaces stays in Restore Backup), or when the farm was also played on another device, with a Choose button that takes you to your farms to pick one. Choose a Version shows which game version saved each copy, and your choice now carries to your other devices.
Switching between iPhone and iPad no longer asks which copy to keep when iCloud simply has your newer save, or when the two copies are almost the same.
When a farm really was played on two devices, you're asked once, when you open it. Decide Later takes you back to your farms.

A farm's Properties in Load Game now shows the Game Version that last saved it (and the one that made it, when different). Farms saved before this update show "Not recorded" until they are saved again.

Upgraded tools look upgraded: their metal turns dark gunmetal at Level 2 and purple at Level 3, everywhere the tool is shown, and every tool's handle is now a darker wood. The Fishing Rod is now drawn in the same pixel style as the other tools.
A tool's "Level 2" and "Level 3" text is now gunmetal grey and purple, the colours of its pictures, instead of purple and orange.

Making a new farm now has Advanced Options under its name: Pond Size, Tree Density (Sparse, Default or Dense), Rocks (Fewer, Default or More) and Ore Rarity (Rarer, Default or Common), plus the farm's world seed, which holds every option: changing an option changes the seed, pasting a seed sets the options, and copying it to share gives a friend the same map. Each farm's "..." menu in Load Game now has Properties, showing its options and seed (farms made before today show "Not recorded").

New farms now get 2 or 3 ponds in three set sizes (small, medium and a wide large one), all with the same softly rounded corners, spaced well apart, a little way in from the map's edge and clear of the middle where your farm starts; with 2 they sit in opposite corners of the map. When making a new farm you can pick Small, Default or Large ponds under Advanced Options: bigger ponds hold more ducks and fish and leave fewer trees. Existing farms keep their ponds.
Selected and locked badges now sit on the top-left corner of the item's icon instead of the end of the row; a locked item shows the padlock even if selected.
The farm now stays on screen until the Load Game menu has fully opened, instead of being cleared as soon as the circle closes over it.
Catching an ordinary orange firefly now counts in Progress: Environment has a Firefly entry beside the colored ones, and one you already hold is credited.
Fireworks now only play when you level up; placing the first building of a kind no longer sets them off.
Each night now grows 4 to 6 trees instead of 5 to 7. Existing trees stay.

New farms look like they used to: ponds, trees and rocks as before, with only easy ones near the start (nothing your first Axe or Pickaxe can't clear within 5 tiles of the first fields, nothing needing the best tools within 10). Ponds can lie anywhere again but never come out square, and new farms start with Copper and Silver veins. Existing farms are unchanged.
On iPad the tutorial checklist no longer stretches across the whole screen; it stays a compact, centered panel like on a phone.
On iPad the Money and Level badges now scale up with the rest of the on-screen controls.
On iPad a tool's choice list now opens beside its tool circle instead of off to one side.
Music now starts as soon as the game opens and keeps playing on the Load Game and New Game menu, in the season of the farm you last played.
The tutorial now waits until a new or loaded farm is fully on screen, after the opening circle, before showing its steps.
The tutorial's fishing steps now point you to the nearest common fish, the easiest to catch, and put one in a pond if there is none.
Tapping a greyed Upgrade button now also tells you what the upgrade will cost.

Trees no longer grow bigger over time: each keeps the size it appeared at, or the one you pick from the new Size dropdown when planting it (Small, Medium, Big or Huge, a bigger one costing more, and destroying one refunds 80% of what its size cost), and Progress collects each tree color at each size.
Trees, rocks and ore veins that need a better Axe or Pickaxe no longer appear near your starting fields, on a new farm or overnight, and they get more common toward the edges of the map.
Trees that appear overnight now come in every size, from Small to Huge, instead of only Small and Medium.
The fish you catch now always shows below the "You caught" pill, also while the tutorial list pushes the pill down.
The Bucket now catches the usual orange fireflies as well as the colored ones: each goes into Storage as a Firefly, earns a Common one's XP, and can be set free again at night.
Every new farm now starts with at least one rare fish in its ponds.

Load Game now closes your farm and opens a menu on the carrot screen, newest farm first: tap a farm to open it, start a New Farm with a name you type (Create waits for one no other farm uses), or rename, restore a backup of or delete any farm, with the iCloud button in the corner. The game also opens on this menu when yours can't be opened, and never makes a farm for you. With no farm (a first launch, or after you delete your last one) it opens on "New Game" with the name field ready, and Create waits for a name.
On a new farm, ponds now sit near the edges and corners of the map, with a few tiles of grass between each pond and the edge.
Fruit trees in the Progress crops list now show the tree full of ripe fruit instead of a basket of the fruit.

iCloud no longer switches the farm you're playing, or the one you open the game on, to another copy by itself: when iCloud has a different copy of it, you're asked which to keep, with each copy's last played time, level, money, play time, day and device, and the other stays in Restore Backup. An old copy saved again on another device no longer counts as newer when it is behind.

Ore veins of every kind, gold, ruby and sapphire included, can now be found from the start and come back overnight; copper is still the most common and sapphire the rarest, and a better Pickaxe is what lets you mine the rarer ones.

Every message the tutorial shows is now its own step in its list, with its own check: zooming in on a tree, rock, ore vein or fish once it is on screen, and selling or keeping a fish once it is caught.
Fishing no longer shows a green ring on the fish while you hold the rod over it.

The tutorial checklist shows only the step you're on, one row tall with as much room above its words as below and a slightly bigger cap with a little more room above it, keeps one size through the whole tutorial, and sits a little lower.
The placement confirm button now says Build when placing a building and Place for everything else.

The tutorial now waits for you to pick the Pet House in the Build list before saying "Tap anywhere on your farm to build it"; opening the list or picking another building no longer skips ahead, and the finger points at the Pet House row.

Every night now has 1 to 3 colored fireflies, the rest the usual orange, in every butterfly color including a new deep orange Legendary Firefly: Uncommon is the most likely, then Rare, Epic, Common and Legendary, and the shifting one the rarest; Progress no longer has a separate Fireflies entry, only one for each color.
The tutorial's "Find" steps now only count a tree, rock, ore vein or fish as found once it is clear of the step list, the money and Level, and the tool bar, not hidden under them.
The Progress Environment panel now heads its colored fireflies "Fireflies" instead of "Night".
Butterflies are now named "Rare Butterfly" and so on in Progress, instead of "Rare Wings", matching the fireflies.

The tutorial now has you plant Carrots on all your farmland, the original tiles as well as the new ones: "Plant Carrots" counts the empty tiles, and if Wheat is still on a tile, steps of their own have you harvest it, switch back to Carrot Seeds and "Plant Carrots on all your farmland" until every tile has Carrots (8/8).
Tapping a fish with the Fishing Rod now casts at it wherever its shadow is, even while it swims between tiles, instead of only on the tile it was in.
New farms start the tutorial straight away with no question first, and Exit Tutorial now asks you to confirm before turning it off.
The gain pill that shows XP, money and items before they fly into the totals now sits below the tutorial's step list while the tutorial shows.
In the tutorial's second Wheat round, once the Wheat you planted again has grown, a step of its own now has you switch to the Scythe before selecting Store Mode and harvesting the Wheat into Storage.

The tutorial now says "Find a small tree", "Find a small rock" and the like for each thing it has you find, and its planting steps read "Plant Wheat", "Plant more Wheat" and "Plant Carrots" with their counts, without the farmland wording.

The lists that open from a tool (crops, harvest tools, fertilizer, terrain, buildings and decorations) now run across the screen, centered, with tighter spacing so full names fit without being cut off.

The Level-Up screen now stays until you tap Continue, even if you leave the game and come back or open something new from it (closing that menu brings you back to it), and the tutorial's pointing finger no longer shows over it.

A tree, rock or vein too big for your Axe or Pickaxe now says "Upgrade your Pickaxe to Level 2 to harvest this Silver Vein", and its tool button opens the Harvest list at that tool, where its Upgrade button is; a tool whose next upgrade is still locked shows a greyed Upgrade button that says the level it unlocks at.
The notifications question now comes up while the game is loading, before your farm and the tutorial appear, instead of after your first planting.
Tips after the tutorial now start on their own as they come due, with no question first; closing one asks whether you want to keep getting tips.

During the tutorial a checklist topped by the tutorial's cap runs across the top of the screen under your money and Level, showing the step you're on in full with its live count; once it is done its circle fills with a green check as it fades out, and the next step slides in from below. It replaces the tutorial's hint bubbles above the tools, and its Exit Tutorial button leaves the tutorial. Until the tutorial ends, messages, banners, the fishing meter, your catch and the arrow toward things off screen show below the list instead of over it.
Picking Water (or any other row) from a tool's list and quickly tapping the farm behind it no longer switches the tool back to Farmland or another row of the closing list.

Farmland beside new water, or new farmland beside water, now soaks up the water one tile at a time over a few seconds, as it already did around a new sprinkler, and dries out the same way when the water or sprinkler goes; a tile only grows crops faster once it looks wet.

The tutorial's hints are reworded and shorter, you switch to the right tool before going to find each thing to gather, closing Storage is part of switching back to Sell Mode, which no longer ends with a message about Store Mode, and the planting steps count only tiles with the crop they ask for.
The tutorial now waits until you have harvested all the ripe Wheat, and sold all the Wheat in Storage, before moving on, counting as you go.

Carrots now grow in 30 seconds ($0.14 seed, $0.30 sale, 3 XP) and Potatoes in 1 minute ($0.33 seed, $0.66 sale, 4 XP), so three harvests of a full field of each level's newest crop take you to the next level.

Every tool can now reach Level 3 by player Level 10, for much less: Axe 2 at Level 3 ($100), Scythe 2 at 4 ($200), Bucket 2 at 5 ($300), Pickaxe 2 and Fishing Rod 2 at 6 ($500, $250), Axe 3 at 7 ($900), Scythe 3 and Fishing Rod 3 at 8 ($1,200, $600), Bucket 3 at 9 ($1,500) and Pickaxe 3 at 10 ($2,000).
Chickens, roosters too, count in Progress once grown up
Upgraded House and Market Stand now count in Progress
Each colored firefly now has its own Progress entry
Carrots now grow in 20 seconds and cost and sell for less ($0.11 seed, $0.22 sale, 1 XP), earning about the same money over time, so the tutorial can afford Carrots for your whole field.
Coming back to the game now carries the rain or snow on from where it was, with the drops in the same places, instead of starting the fall again.

The tutorial never runs out of things to gather for the Pet House: if no tree, rock or Copper Vein your tools can cut is left, small pines, a small rock or a Copper Vein appear near your field, and it points only at ones your tools can cut.
A tree or rock too big for your Axe or Pickaxe now shakes when refused, and its message stays up for 4 seconds so there is time to read it.
Market Stand ore quests now ask only for ore your Pickaxe can mine, and the bars and cut gems made from it.
Tapping anything in Progress explains how to collect it, or what you did
Every fourth wind wisp now curls the other way, bending down instead of up.
Trees are now planted from the Decorate tool instead of Terrain, and cost money: Pine $20, Birch $40, Oak $60. Destroying a planted tree gives back 80% of its price.
You can now place a Pet House for every cat and dog, 15 in all, so one of each fits on the farm.
Sprinkler now costs $100 (was $400) and Big Sprinkler $500 (was $1,600).
Animals no longer have a shadow under their feet; the pond fish keep their dark silhouettes.
Very rarely a firefly glows in a butterfly color instead of orange: catch it with the Bucket, and set it free again from Storage at night, where it flits about its spot every night and hides by day.
The Axe and Pickaxe pages, their upgrade pages and the level-up screen now say what each level can fell or mine, and how many logs, stones and ore it gives.

Bigger wild trees need a better Axe and bigger rocks and rarer veins a better Pickaxe: Axe 1 fells Small trees, Axe 2 adds Medium and Big, Axe 3 adds Huge; Pickaxe 1 breaks Small rocks and Copper, Pickaxe 2 adds Medium rocks, Silver and Gold, Pickaxe 3 adds Big rocks, Ruby and Sapphire. Trees you planted and rocks you placed always come down. Veins no longer sometimes drop a bonus piece of ore.
Settings has a drawn steel gear icon on the tool ring instead of a plain white gear.
Storage has a drawn backpack icon on the tool ring and in its menu: tan with a dark brown leather flap, carry loop, strap and pocket and a brass buckle.
Tap anything the level-up screen says you unlocked to jump to its menu.
Common fish now swim faster and take longer to catch, and every rarer fish is still harder than them.
Pond fish shadows are smaller and no longer breathe.

New Gameplay setting "Open Tool Menu on Select" (on by default): turn it off and picking a tool no longer opens its list; tap the tool's chip beside the circle to open it. The tutorial still opens it.
Storage no longer shows Trash (or Release) on items you can sell, such as crops and fish; logs, stones and butterflies keep theirs.

While fishing, tapping the fish now says "Drag the fishing rod over the fish to catch it.", and tapping it again shows the hand dragging the rod onto it; taps on the water no longer reach the farm underneath or say there is no fish there.
At level 5, if you have never opened the Progress menu, the tutorial offers a quick tip to tap Level and see your progress.
The Pet House now also takes one Copper Ore, and the tutorial mines it from a Copper Vein.
A new farm now always starts with at least two Copper Veins among its ore veins.
Tapping a fence now says to use the Axe unless you are holding it (the Decorate tool still places and removes fences).

The tutorial no longer asks you to pinch while the Wheat grows; instead, once you reach level 2 and before you get the Axe, a two-finger animation shows you how to pinch to zoom out and see your whole farm.

When what the tutorial points at is off screen it now says "Let's go find a tree." or "Let's go find another tree." (likewise rocks and ore veins) instead of telling you to drag the farm, with the same arrow at the edge.
The tutorial now has you switch to Farmland and "Tap anywhere on your farm to place it" for all the new farmland your level allows, counting the tiles.
The fishing tutorial now says "Drag the fishing rod over the fish to catch it."

A success sound now plays as you finish each main step of the tutorial, such as planting, harvesting logs, stones and ore, and building, but not for finding things or catching a fish, which has its own sound.
The tutorial's planting steps now ask you to plant Wheat on all your farmland, counting the tiles as you go, and the second round says "Plant more Wheat seeds".
When the tutorial first asks for a tool it now says "Now switch to the Axe." (likewise the Scythe, Pickaxe, Fishing Rod and Farmland).
The tutorial now says "Let's build a Pet House." and, once Build is picked, "Tap anywhere on your farm to build it."
Finishing the tutorial now shows a Tutorial Complete message saying it will chime in as you unlock features like quests and stock trading.
Fences now join up cleanly in the same look: a post every half tile with rails between, across and up and down the farm, and tidy corners, junctions and ends.

Wool, Flour, Bread, Planks, Cloth and Bricks have real pictures instead of emoji, and the juices, preserves, pickles, soup, pie and roasted coffee now look like what they are instead of potted plants.
Each time the tutorial waits on the Wheat it now says "Wait on the Wheat to grow" with the seconds left, and moves on only once the Wheat is ripe.
Fixed iCloud sync getting stuck on "Couldn't reach iCloud" after a farm was played on two devices while apart; the other device's copy is kept in Restore Backup when you need to choose.

After level 2 the tutorial now has you build the Pet House and adopt a pet first, then add farmland and plant Carrots on it, then fish. The tutorial also no longer points at a tree, rock or ore vein hidden behind a tree.

The tutorial now says to tap the grass for farmland, and for logs, stones and ore it has you switch to the tool, find a tree, rock or ore vein with the arrow, then tap it, such as "Tap the tree with the Axe to harvest logs (2/6)."
When what the tutorial points at is off screen it now shows only an arrow at the edge of the screen, and when it is too small it only says to zoom in, with no hand dragging or pinching the farm.
The fishing tutorial now has you switch to the Fishing Rod, find a fish, tap it to start fishing, then drag the tool circle onto it, with the same steady hand as planting and no filling ring.
While the first Wheat grows the tutorial now has you pinch to zoom in and out, still counting down the seconds.
The tutorial now has you place the Pet House near your farmland, with the arrow pointing there.
The tutorial now says "Select the Scythe." and then "Select Store Mode." when it is time to switch the Scythe to Store.
Two farms can no longer have the same name: a name already in use is turned away with a short message, and farms that already shared one get a number such as "Farm 1 (2)".
Load Game now lists your farms in alphabetical order by name, with "My Farm (2)" before "My Farm (10)".
New farms you don't name are now called "My Farm" instead of "Farm 1", "Farm 2" and so on, with a number such as "My Farm (2)" when that name is taken; farms you already have keep their names.
The Source Code link is gone from the About menu.
Red new dots in the menus now go away once you have seen the item on screen, not only when you tap it.
Decorations and other things you have from the start no longer get a red new dot; only things you unlock later, such as by levelling up, do.
Decorations and other unlocked items no longer look greyed out like locked ones when you can't afford them yet; their missing money or materials show in red instead.
The Market Stand now comes only as its full yellow stand, since the other colors were just a roof, and stands built in those colors now show it too.
Grown crops whose pictures are bigger, such as ripe Wheat, Leeks and Tomatoes, now keep their shape and stand taller instead of being squeezed into their spot.
After the tutorial, each tip (the Market Stand, the Stock Market, the Tractor) now asks first, such as "Want a quick tutorial for the Tractor?": Show me starts it and No thanks puts it away for good.
Wheat now grows in 10 seconds and sells for $0.10 (still $0.60 a minute) and earns 1 XP instead of 2, so reaching level 2 still takes 12 harvests.

The Pet House now unlocks at level 2, needs 6 logs instead of 15 (still 2 stones) and costs no money, every one of them: it only takes its logs and stones, its menus say Free, and taking one down gives back only materials.

A new farm's Scythe starts on Sell, and the tutorial now has you cut your first Wheat that way, then plant again, switch to Store, cut it into Storage, sell it from there, close Storage and switch back to Sell. Farms you already have keep their choice.

The tips are now a tutorial that runs start to finish: after the Wheat it lets you farm freely, saying only to keep farming until level 2, where the farmland chapter starts by itself, and at the end it says you have completed the tutorial. Fishing is now its last chapter, after your pet, with a fish put in a pond for it, and turning the tutorial back on no longer starts it over.
Selling Wheat from Storage in the tutorial now has the hand show you each tap: the tool, Storage, Sell on the Wheat, Max to sell all of it, Sell, then Close.
The tutorial now also has you break an ore vein with the Pickaxe, then tap your new Pet House and pick its pet one choice at a time: cat or dog, its breed (and a dog's color), a name, then OK.

Each step of the tutorial and the tips now says only what it is for, in one plain sentence such as "Chop trees for logs (2/6).", which stays the same while the hand shows each tap, and the tool circle is called the tool.
The tutorial's pointing hand no longer draws a gold ring where the tool lands as it drags.

Tips are now called the Tutorial: a new farm asks if you want a quick tutorial, Settings → Gameplay has a Tutorial switch and, once you have finished it, a Replay Tutorial button, and the x on its bubble turns the tutorial off, while on a later tip it closes just that tip.
Once the tutorial is done and your House stands, a tip shows you how to open the Stock Market, look up a ticker and buy shares, then sell some. It waits while you are offline.
After the tutorial, new tips show you how to build and open the Market Stand once you can afford one, and how to send a Tractor out harvesting and unload what it brings back once you have one.
In the Pet House menu, a cat's dropdown is now called Breed instead of Color, since its choices are kinds of cat.

The tutorial no longer has steps of its own for zooming and looking around, and never moves the camera: when what it points at is off screen or too small to tap, an arrow at the edge of the screen points to it and the hand shows dragging or pinching the farm to bring it into view.

In the tutorial, a tree is now chopped by tapping it with the Axe, a rock or an ore vein broken by tapping it with the Pickaxe, and the Pet House put down by tapping open grass, and the hand taps too instead of rubbing or dragging.
The tutorial now waits for your finger to lift before it moves on to the next step.
While your Wheat grows, the tutorial counts down the seconds until it is ripe.

Loading another farm, starting a new one, restoring the farm you are playing from a backup or taking a newer copy of it from iCloud now closes the menus and plays the same loading screen and opening circle as starting the game, instead of swapping the farm in at once.
A new farm starts with only copper and silver veins; gold, ruby and sapphire veins turn up later, with the veins that appear overnight.

The Grid Lines switch in Settings → Graphics is now a Hide Grid Lines Beyond slider: grid lines fade out as you zoom out and are gone past the zoom you pick (3.5× to start), all the way left hides them and all the way right always shows them. The lines are also a little thinner. If you had turned grid lines off, they stay off.

Decoration looks that were cut wrongly from their pictures are gone: the Market Accessories' register, scale and fish sign, the Woodworking Supplies' tool board and the Baking Supplies' four bread pots. Any you already placed or stored become a market sign, a hacksaw or a loaf of bread.

Decorations and sprinklers no longer unlock with levels: each now costs its price plus one or two things from storage that match what it is made of, such as logs for the Wooden Table, stones and logs for the Well, Wheat and logs for the Scarecrow, a Copper Bar for the Weathercock, a Pumpkin for the Pumpkin, Copper Ore and stones for a Sprinkler, a Polished Ruby for the Decorative Chest and a Polished Sapphire for the Crafting Supplies. Their rows and pages show what you have against what is needed in green or red, a missing one is named when you try to place it, destroying one gives back 80% of its materials as well as its money, and the Level-Up screen no longer lists decorations.

Breaking an ore vein now drops pieces of ore with pictures of their own (Copper, Silver and Gold Ore, Rough Ruby and Rough Sapphire) instead of a picture of the vein, and the Stone Oven's bars and the DIY Crafting Table's polished gems now look like bars and cut gems.

Ore veins now drop a lot that fits their kind (6 Copper Ore, 5 Silver, 4 Gold, 3 rough gems, 3 from a Small Silver Vein), every vein takes six swings, one vein in five drops a piece more, and raw ore sells for $6 to $50 a piece by rarity instead of $8 for all.

Smelting and cutting now take one vein's worth and pay double: 5 Copper Ore make a $60 Copper Bar in 6 minutes, 5 Silver Ore a $100 Silver Bar in 8, 4 Gold Ore a $144 Gold Bar in 10, and one rough ruby or sapphire is cut into an $80 Polished Ruby or a $100 Polished Sapphire in 5.
From level 18 the Market Stand also asks for ore, bars and polished gems.
The Pickaxe's page now says what veins give and how often a bonus piece drops.
Ore and polished gems chime like a gem when they are gathered; bars still come out of the Stone Oven with the cooking sound.
On the Level-Up screen, the farmland you gained is now a "Farmland" card like the others, with its picture, name and numbers in the same layout, instead of a pill of its own.
Collecting fruit with the Bucket no longer makes the fruit tree flicker through cut-up, mirrored pictures; the tree now gives a short wobble instead.

A new farm now asks on its first load whether you would like to see tips on basic game mechanics as you play; turn them on or off any time with Settings → Gameplay → Tips (turned back on, they carry on where they stopped, or start over once you have seen them all), or hide them with the x on a tip's bubble. Once the Wheat is planted they show how to pinch the farm to zoom and drag it to look around, moving on when you do. After the Wheat they also show how to set the Scythe to Sell and sell crops as you cut them, and, once a level unlocks more, how to lay Farmland beside your field, then, once the Pet House unlocks, how to cut logs with the Axe, break stones with the Pickaxe and put the Pet House up, and, when a fish is in a pond, how to cast the Fishing Rod onto it, hold it over the fish until the bar fills and sell or keep the catch (this takes the place of the one-time "Hold the rod over the fish" line in the Catch Meter). Tips show each step with a pointing finger that taps the one thing to tap next (which glows and wears the red dot, in Storage as well as beside the tool circle), or drags the tool circle out over the farm along a dotted trail, so dragging and tapping are plain to tell apart; when picking a tool opens its list, it first taps what to take from it (Wheat Seeds, the Scythe, Farmland, the Axe, the Pickaxe, the Pet House or the Fishing Rod); the farm glides into view when what it points at is off screen. With Reduce Motion the finger stands still at the end of its trail.

On iOS 26 and later your farms sync through iCloud, so you can start on one device and carry on on another: at launch, when you come back to the game, and every couple of minutes while you play, so a farm left open on one device can be picked up on another. The cloud button at the top of Load Game shows whether they are synced and syncs when tapped; if iCloud is off for Stock Farmer, needs iOS 26 or can't be reached, it says so and what to do. Load Game says which device each farm was last played on, by the device's model (such as "iPhone 16 Pro"), and, when a farm was played on two devices, shows both copies side by side with what each is ahead on and which is the most recent, so you can keep one; the other stays in Restore Backup. The game never waits for iCloud: offline or with iCloud off, it saves on the device as before, and it catches up by itself once you are back online.
A short message now tells you when syncing with iCloud keeps failing or stock prices can't be updated, once rather than every time, without stopping play.
The "Your latest changes could not be saved" panel no longer flashes up for a moment during play: it shows only when saving keeps failing for a while, and goes as soon as a save works again.
Fish in ponds now turn back to face left or right as soon as they finish swimming up or down, so they always rest sideways.
Common fish change direction more often and sometimes double back, so they are a little harder to land.
The Water page now says that big ponds get fish to catch with the Fishing Rod and that ducks come to them on their own.
The walk through on a new farm now ends once you sell your first Wheat, with no Max or Close steps to tap, and it catches up on its own when you do a step early or lose your Wheat on the way.

The Level-Up screen is redesigned: a big "LEVEL UP" with the purple level number appears with the fireworks without stopping play while the rest of the screen's buttons and pills slip out of the way until you tap Continue, then the details fade in under it (once you lift your finger, if you were dragging a tool), headed "Now unlocked" in a list that scrolls when it is long, with Continue always in view: the farmland you gained, then every new crop, building, decoration, recipe, upgrade and kind of fish with its picture and key numbers in the same colors as the tool lists.
Settings → About now shows the release's version and build number, and a long press on it copies them for a bug report.

Item, building and upgrade pages are shorter: each shows its key numbers as rows (cost, sale price, time, XP, limit, what an upgrade changes) in one set of colors used in the lists too, with at most two short notes, and times read "Grows in 1m".
Locked items in the tool lists now show their whole row greyed out, including the name, even when you could afford them (Pumpkin was one that did not).

Sounds are rebalanced and quieter overall (at 100%, Music, Effects and Ambience now play as loud as 80%, 75% and 70% did), harvesting and other drag sounds no longer drown out the menus and buttons, and the music softly lowers while the level-up, quest and all-crops-ready fanfares play.
Sound settings are now Master, Music, Effects and Ambience (Interface, Farm and Animals are joined as Effects); the sliders work evenly across their range and change sounds that are already playing.
Trees and rocks you place yourself give no logs or stone when you chop or break them, even with full storage, and do not count as mined; only the ones that grew on their own do.
The Career screen is now called Progress.
Ducks no longer lay eggs and make no sound; tap a duck and Sell it for $25 instead of releasing it, while every other animal still offers Release. Duck eggs already in storage stay there.
Harvesting into Storage now makes the same sound as selling the harvest, and so does the Tractor storing its load.
Planting now starts the instant you drag a seed one button width, with no extra wait.
The first planting drag on a new farm is no longer interrupted; the question about notifications now waits until you lift your finger.
The Time sheet no longer shows the line about when night lasts.
The loading screen now also waits for the sound effects, rain and music to load, so the first sounds play without a stutter.
Removed the Dynamic Shadows setting and its intensity slider from Graphics settings; shadows from buildings, trees and the like are gone for good (animals keep the shadow under their feet).
A message that a farm could not be opened, created, renamed, deleted or restored now stays until you retry or try again, instead of vanishing with the next autosave.
Music is half as loud as it was.
The startup screen shows the carrot icon again, and its loading bar now fills smoothly instead of jumping and flickering.
Sounds now pan gently left or right by where they are on screen.

Sound settings now have Interface, Farm, Animals and Ambience, each with its own volume shown as a percentage instead of a switch (0% is off): animals (calls, petting, the cat's trill) are no longer part of Farm sounds.
Opening the game shows the carrot app icon and a loading bar, then a circle opens onto your fully loaded farm; Reduce Motion uses a gentle fade.

Every sound is balanced by type (animals a little louder than other farm sounds, fanfares a little louder, menu clicks and the night chime quieter, rain and music evened out) and all the volume sliders now start at 100%.

Only animal sounds get quieter as you zoom out or look away from them (full volume only while zoomed well in, 40% fully zoomed out and never below 10%); every other farm sound stays at full volume wherever it happens.
Animals you are zoomed in on and can see (not while they shelter inside for the night, rain or snow) call out now and then on their own, one kind at a time and not often; cats only ever trill.

Settings has Timelapse: save a farm screenshot each in-game day at your chosen time, play or scrub through them with crossfade or instant transitions, check their size, clear them or turn recording off.
Ducks lay eggs without eating, every 10 minutes (slower than hens), and the countdown for the next egg starts once you take it with the Bucket.
A Chicken Coop holds 2 chickens at Level 1, 4 at Level 2 and 6 at Level 3.
Fish in Storage have Release instead of Trash, and Storage's Equip button now says Select.
Every Upgrade button just says Upgrade and opens a page with the details and the button that buys it; the Career's Home Upgrades are now Building Upgrades.
The Tractor's countdown reads "Ready in" with the time left.
The Cuddle Clouds song is gone.

The Time sheet has preset buttons (Midnight, Morning, Midday, Rain, Evening, Night) instead of a slider, with a sky picture that matches the time; Midnight sets 12:01 AM and starts the new-day animation, and the other times no longer trigger extra new days, chimes or waves.
Trees, rocks and ores that the new-day wave grows now fade in with a brief gentle glow in the wave's color.
Tapping a farm animal now offers Release instead of Sell: it leaves for no money or XP.
Releasing a butterfly has its own sound, and anything equipped from Storage shows how many are left after its name, in red as (x0) once you run out.
The Storage buttons are wider, so Release has room around its text.
Taking eggs, milk, wool or fertilizer from animals now earns XP, more for animals that unlock later.
The Tractor's crops now give their XP when you store or sell the load, along with the cash from a sale, instead of when it picks them up.
The new-day chime is tried again if it is dropped, so it plays every night.

Butterflies can be caught with the Bucket for XP, kept in Storage, equipped and released back onto the farm, up to 10 at a time; released butterflies stay, never leave and rest in one spot at night and in rain or snow.
Butterfly wing colors in Career now count when you catch one.

Every new day animation grows new trees, rocks and ores as the wave passes (5 to 7 trees, 2 to 3 rocks and an ore), spread evenly all the way round the map and mostly toward its edge, instead of them coming back while you are away.
A fish you place never disappears, even if you let it go on the tile another fish started from.
Petting or harvesting an animal no longer turns it or changes how it stands: it keeps walking, grazing or resting the way it was.
Sheep are sheared with the Scythe instead of the Bucket.
Farmland no longer has a cap: levels 2 to 19 unlock twice their number in tiles and every level from 20 on unlocks as many tiles as its number, for 657 tiles by level 30.
Harvest quests never ask for more than 100 of a crop, and a second crop from the Scythe upgrade counts toward them.
The fall sky is darker with a brownish-orange tint.
Fireworks only go off when you level up.
Paths and grass can go under buildings and decorations, and any terrain under a sprinkler.
Paths cost $2 a tile; grass and farmland stay free.
The new-day wave is green in spring, orange in fall and light blue in winter, and rolls out from the middle of your screen.
Closing or backgrounding the app during the new-day animation no longer replays it or skips a day.
The Axe takes fences down into Storage, and stored fences can be equipped and placed.
The Tractor drives over farmland, finishes each connected plot of farmland before moving on, and can reach any ripe crop, even one in front of a pet house.
The Tractor harvests only the ripe plants of a crop, and its Harvest button shows as soon as some are ready.

The Tractor's load shows as a crop and count floating over it. Harvest it with the Scythe, which flies it to your totals like any other crop, or sell or store it from the Tractor's menu, at any time, even while it drives. It has to be emptied before the next trip.
The Tractor makes a pickup sound when you are zoomed in close enough to see it work.
Chickens and livestock step away from a driving Tractor.
A crop tile feeds animals four times, and each meal removes one of the four crop pictures on the tile.
The Tractor's load floats a bit higher over it, and eggs over hens are about 10% smaller and float a bit higher.
Placing, destroying and cancelling use the words Place, Destroy and Cancel, and Storage rows say Trash.
Button text is white on grey buttons, dark green on green buttons and dark red on red buttons in every menu.
Removed the song Tales from the Vienna Woods.

Dropdown list rows show how many you have placed out of the most allowed, such as Pet House (3/10) and Farmland (30/100), and prices in the Terrain, Decorate and Fertilize lists look like building prices.
Sound, Graphics and Gameplay settings each have a Reset to Defaults button at the bottom.
In the Build and Decorate lists, items that come in several looks or colors cycle through them; picking one still uses its usual look and the tool button does not cycle.

Chicken Coops, Rabbit Hutches, Sheep, Goat and Pig Barns, Stables and Luxury Barns now start with 4 animals and can be upgraded with a purple Upgrade button to 7 and then 10, each upgrade unlocking at its own level from 7 to 24; the Career menu lists the levels reached.

Leveling up opens a screen listing what the level brings: new crops, farmland tiles, buildings, decorations, trees, recipes, tool and building upgrades, new kinds of fish and when rarer fish become more likely.

Added a Changelog to the About menu, first in the list. It has a search bar, a calendar button to pick a day or a range of days, days that fold away with only the latest open, and pages of seven days with Newer and Older buttons at the bottom. GitHub in the About menu is now called Source Code.
The Tractor finishes connected farmland before driving to separated farmland, and its menu lists crops by what they pay.

Every harvest tool has two upgrades: the Axe fells trees in fewer hits, the Scythe and Bucket sometimes give a second item, the Pickaxe breaks rocks in fewer hits and the Fishing Rod widens its circle.
Fish rarer than common ones become more likely every five levels up to level 30.

Added the Career menu from the level panel, with collections for crops, fish, animals, buildings, decorations, terrain, recipes, environment and tools, charts for level and money, and search and filters.
Finished quests are turned in automatically with a banner and the XP flying into the level panel.
Every building is limited to one except Pet Houses, Chicken Coops, Sheds and Silos, and the Barn is split into Sheep, Goat and Pig Barns.
Sprinklers can be set to spray all the time, and the first building of each kind sets off fireworks.
Messages and banners appear in the middle of the screen.
Terrain replaces other terrain and leaves fences standing.
The Axe stores decorations, and any stored item can be equipped: decorations are set down for free, fish are released into water and crops are dragged onto animals to feed them.
Storage rows show the name and count on one line with full-width Equip, Sell and Trash buttons.
Animals that give something to harvest graze on their favorite crop in the field and give nothing until they have eaten, and stay fed until you harvest them.
Pigs, rabbits and donkeys give only fertilizer, and hens hold one egg that floats over them.
Moving a building or decoration only needs its bottom row on the map.
Planting choices are named by what you plant, such as Potato Tubers.
The Settings menu is a list of Load Game, Screenshot Farm, Sound, Graphics, Gameplay, Performance and About.
Butterflies land on individual crop sprites.

Added fishing as a game: cast the Fishing Rod on a fish, hold the rod over it while the Catch Meter fills, then sell or store it. Fish have weights, rarities, XP and a price up to $1,000, and fight harder as the bar fills.
Uncommon and rare fish appear from level 10, epic from 15 and legendary from 20.
Added the Tractor: a live overview of planted crops, harvest trips that drive over your farm, cargo you sell or store at home, and four facings.
Added a Dynamic Shadows setting (off by default) with an intensity slider.
Added pixel butterflies by day and wind curls past leaning trees; rain and snow lean with the wind.
Music, Menu Sounds, Farm Sounds and Ambience each have a toggle and a volume slider.
Added a Grid Lines setting and a Screenshot Farm button that saves your whole farm to Photos.
Fish and ducks spawn on any water by its shape, and ducks can walk between ponds.
The farm's clock holds still while the app is closed or in the background.
Decorations can layer over each other by bottom row only, and dropdown items already placed as many times as allowed are greyed out.
Item menus are ordered by unlock level.
Animals are no longer held in by a roaming limit; fences are what keep them in.
Added the four seasons (Spring, Fall and Winter) with their own pictures for everything on the farm, chosen on the Time sheet.
Added soft shadows from the sun for everything standing on the farm.
Added 39 groups of farmyard decorations with many looks, the Dairy, Cotton and Cloth, artisan recipes, ore veins and gems with processing, and Birch trees.
Added ten more crops after Blackberry, so the last crop is Coffee at level 34, and every song is spread across the seasons.
Added a Cobblestone Path and a Dirt Path, and a Big Sprinkler upgrade that reaches 3 tiles.
Added a Tool Offset setting that moves where a dragged tool works.
Added Market Stand colors that carry through upgrades.
Fish are caught only with the Fishing Rod.
Ducks leave a pixel wake on the water.
Livestock walk using their walking animation.
Animals stand in the middle of their tile with their shadow under them.
Cows roam from the Luxury Barn entrance and return to shelter.
Added Market quests: the Market Stand offers random quests for XP, and the large Market Stand is a purple upgrade after ten finished quests.

Added the Stock Market in your House: search for tickers, buy and sell shares with live prices from Yahoo Finance, see day change and overall performance, and use a Luxury House upgrade for ten stock slots.
Added Stock Market quests that ask you to earn a profit.
Added sprinklers that spray water on a schedule, soak the land around them and dry it out again when they are moved or destroyed.
Farmland is capped at 500 tiles by level 24, and the slowest crop takes 2 hours.
Buildings, fruit trees, decorations and trees can be picked up and moved by holding a finger on them, and destroying gives back 80%.
Things can be set down over the upper tiles of one another, taking up only their bottom row, and everything is drawn in order by how far down the map it stands.
Saves are protected: unreadable saves are reported, each save slot keeps an older backup, and a daily backup advances when the farm's day rolls.
Load Game lists up to ten saved games with a New Game button and shows real play time.
The dragged tool works a fixed distance up and to the right of the circle, and every tool starts after the same drag distance.
Rain falls from 2 PM to 5 PM.
Hens' wheat only speeds up laying, using up one wheat per egg.
Added the midnight wave of glowing pixels with a chime, and a few fireflies that drift out on deep nights.
Added fish in ponds, caught with the Bucket into Storage.
Replaced the tools menu with a ring of buttons around the tool circle, where a tool fans out its choices and the green i opens an item's page.
Added a farm day counter and a banner at midnight that lists what sold the day before.
A building's money, logs and stones show under its name in its dropdown, green or red, and crops show grow time and reward.
Dropdown lists run across the width of a phone and open above the tool.
Sound effects and animals sheltering from rain were tuned.
Added rocks, stones and the Pickaxe: buildings now cost logs and stones.
Added dogs in Pet Houses and livestock: rabbits, ducks, sheep, goats, pigs, donkeys and cows.
Added workshops and the Market Stand, the Grain Machine, Silo, Stone Oven, Woodwork Bench, Tailor Table, DIY Crafting Table and Drinking Trough.
Added decorations: Scarecrow, Sprinkler, Well, Trunk, Pumpkins, Wooden Table and Weathercock.
Added a day and night cycle with glowing water, torch-lit buildings and a farm clock in the tools menu.
Added rain, forest sounds and bird calls, and animals go in for the night and the rain.
Hens lay three eggs, and fruit trees take three grow cycles.
Menus and the HUD use dark glass.
Every animal makes its own sound when tapped.
Added hens' eggs, collected with the Harvest tool, and trees to place with a pond-and-forest map.
Added fruit trees after every third crop, and a walk-through that teaches planting wheat, harvesting it and selling it.
Harvesting uses the Scythe, Axe and Bucket, which fill your Storage backpack, and each can store or sell what it gathers.
Added Trash in Storage and trees that grow from Small to Huge.
Added the iPad layout and a launch screen.
Added fertilizer: $10 a tile, 10% faster growth, used up with the crop.
Added the draggable tool circle with Plant, Harvest, Fertilize, Terrain and Build tools, and a red dot for new unlocks.
Added Storage buildings and the Storage backpack, with chickens stored by color.
Added four save slots and a Load Game menu.
Pet houses cost $25 with a limit of 10, and coops cost $250.
Chickens grow up and you are told when they have all grown.
Added buildings you place and move with arrows, OK and Cancel, and a menu for each.
Added pets in Pet Houses and chickens in Chicken Coops, and fences.
The camera position is remembered, and you are notified when the whole field has grown.
Added the farm: planting, growing and harvesting crops, with XP and levels that unlock crops, buildings and farmland.
Added water that makes nearby farmland grow faster, and music and sound effects.
Added cats that wander and ripen crops.
Harvest rewards fly into the HUD.
First version of Stock Farmer: a farm you can plant and harvest, with water, buildings and an app icon.
